title: feat: auto-detect sourceType from URL + derive confidence
body:
Create `src/lib/classify-url.ts` exporting `classifyUrl(url: string): SourceClassification` with priority rules: doi.org/pubmed/scholar → SCIENTIFIC_PAPER; *.edu/*.ac.uk → ACADEMIC_RESOURCE; rhs.org.uk/almanac.com/gardenersworld.com/extension.org/growveg.com/pfaf.org → GARDENING_GUIDE; anything else with URL → BLOG_FORUM. Invalid/unparseable URLs → BLOG_FORUM fallback.

Update `POST /api/relationships` (`src/app/api/relationships/route.ts`) to accept `sources: string[]` (array of URLs). For each URL, create a separate `RelationshipSource` row with `classifyUrl(url)` as sourceType and `SOURCE_CONFIDENCE[sourceType]` as confidence. Always create one testimony row with sourceType=PERSONAL_OBSERVATION, confidence=ANECDOTAL. Relationship confidence = max across all source rows. Keep existing `sourceType` single-field path as fallback for old clients.

Write unit tests in `tests/lib/classify-url.test.ts` covering doi.org, pubmed, .edu, rhs.org.uk, random blog, invalid URL. Write API test for multi-source submission in `tests/api/relationships.test.ts`.

title: feat: show all community sources on relationship detail page
body:
Update `GET /api/plants/[id]/companions/[companionId]` to include `sourceType` and `userId` in the sources select. Do NOT send userId to client; use it only for grouping server-side.

Group community RelationshipSource rows by (userId, date-day of fetchedAt). Each group = one observation: display the testimony row's notes at top, then list URL rows beneath with their sourceType label. Non-community sources (TREFLE, USDA, PFAF) keep existing single-row display.

Add `SOURCE_TYPE_LABELS` in the page component: SCIENTIFIC_PAPER→'Scientific paper', ACADEMIC_RESOURCE→'Academic resource', GARDENING_GUIDE→'Gardening guide', BLOG_FORUM→'Blog / forum', PERSONAL_OBSERVATION→'Personal observation'.

Page: `src/app/plants/[id]/companions/[companionId]/page.tsx`. API route: `src/app/api/plants/[id]/companions/[companionId]/route.ts`. Write tests.

title: feat: evidence quality UI on /contribute — source type input with auto-detection
body:
Redesign the evidence section in `src/app/contribute/page.tsx`.

First check if `src/lib/classify-url.ts` exists. If not, create it (same logic as issue #71: doi.org/pubmed/scholar→SCIENTIFIC_PAPER, *.edu/*.ac.uk→ACADEMIC_RESOURCE, rhs.org.uk/almanac.com etc→GARDENING_GUIDE, else BLOG_FORUM, invalid→BLOG_FORUM).

Add evidence level radio (4 options: 'I observed this personally'=ANECDOTAL, 'I've read about this in resources'=TRADITIONAL, 'I can point to documentation'=OBSERVED, 'I have peer-reviewed sources'=PEER_REVIEWED). This sets the floor.

Replace source input with a list of URL inputs. Each URL row: text input + auto-detected type badge (call classifyUrl on blur) + override select (pre-selected to detected type) + remove button. Show hint: 'doi.org and PubMed links are recognised automatically as scientific papers.'

Update form submission to send `sources: string[]` and `sourceTypeOverrides: Record<number, string>` to POST /api/relationships. The `evidenceLevel` can go into `notes` prefix or be sent as a separate field if the API accepts it.

Write a hook test if any logic is extracted to a custom hook.

title: feat: companion relationship search page + fix relationship URL ordering bug
body:
The search page (`src/app/relationships/page.tsx`), API (`GET /api/relationships?q=&cursor=`), nav link from home, and 404 canonical-order fix are all already implemented on main. Do NOT reimplement them.

Only task remaining: add GET tests to `tests/api/relationships.test.ts`.

Add these test cases to the existing `describe` block (the file already has POST tests — add a new `describe('GET /api/relationships')` block):
1. Returns 200 with array of relationships and no nextCursor when results fit in one page
2. Returns nextCursor when results exceed limit (mock 21 rows, expect nextCursor = last id)
3. Filters by `?q=` — only relationships where cropA or cropB name matches
4. Accepts `?cursor=` and returns only relationships with id < cursor

You need to also mock `prisma.cropRelationship.findMany` in the vi.mock block (it is not currently mocked). Import `GET` from `@/app/api/relationships/route` at the top.

Run `pnpm test:run` via SSH to verify all tests pass before committing.

title: feat: landing hub + global site header (closes #124 #125)
body:
Implement a global site header and replace the home page with a 3-card use-case hub. Also closes #125. DO NOT touch anything under `data/` at any point. ## 1. Transparent logo `logo.png` exists at the repo root with a white background. Strip it to transparency and save as `public/logo.png`. Install sharp: `pnpm add -D sharp`. Then run this one-off script (create, run, delete): ```ts // scripts/strip-logo-bg.ts import sharp from 'sharp' import { resolve } from 'path' import { mkdirSync } from 'fs' mkdirSync('public', { recursive: true }) const { data, info } = await sharp(resolve('logo.png')).ensureAlpha().raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true }) const px = new Uint8Array(data) for (let i = 0; i < px.length; i += 4) { if (px[i] > 238 && px[i+1] > 238 && px[i+2] > 238) px[i+3] = 0 } await sharp(Buffer.from(px), { raw: { width: info.width, height: info.height, channels: 4 } }).png().toFile(resolve('public/logo.png')) ``` Run via SSH: `tsx scripts/strip-logo-bg.ts`. Delete the script after. Commit `public/logo.png`. ## 2. i18n keys Add to `messages/en.json`: ```json "Landing": { "title": "power2plant", "subtitle": "Companion planting garden planner", "lookupTitle": "Look up a crop", "lookupDesc": "Find companions and antagonists for any plant", "planTitle": "Plan beds", "planDesc": "Know what you want to grow — find what fits together", "gardenTitle": "My garden", "gardenDesc": "See how the plants in your beds get along" }, "Nav": { "lookup": "Look up a crop", "plan": "Plan beds", "garden": "My garden" } ``` Add to `messages/de.json`: ```json "Landing": { "title": "power2plant", "subtitle": "Begleitpflanzung — Gartenplaner", "lookupTitle": "Pflanze nachschlagen", "lookupDesc": "Begleiter und Antagonisten für jede Pflanze finden", "planTitle": "Beete planen", "planDesc": "Du weißt, was du anbauen willst — finde, was zusammenpasst", "gardenTitle": "Mein Garten", "gardenDesc": "Schau, wie die Pflanzen in deinen Beeten miteinander auskommen" }, "Nav": { "lookup": "Pflanze nachschlagen", "plan": "Beete planen", "garden": "Mein Garten" } ``` ## 3. SiteHeader component Create `src/components/site-header.tsx`: ```tsx 'use client' import Image from 'next/image' import { Link, usePathname } from '@/i18n/navigation' import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl' import { LocaleSwitcher } from '@/components/locale-switcher' import { AuthPanel } from '@/components/auth-panel' const NAV_ITEMS = [ { key: 'lookup' as const, href: '/relationships' }, { key: 'plan' as const, href: '/plan' }, { key: 'garden' as const, href: '/garden' }, ] satisfies { key: 'lookup' | 'plan' | 'garden'; href: string }[] function isActive(pathname: string, href: string): boolean { if (href === '/relationships') { return pathname.startsWith('/relationships') || pathname.startsWith('/plants') } return pathname === href || pathname.startsWith(href + '/') } export function SiteHeader() { const t = useTranslations('Nav') const pathname = usePathname() return (
power2plant
{NAV_ITEMS.map(({ key, href }) => ( {t(key)} ))}
) } ``` ## 4. Route groups Next.js route groups (folders in parentheses) don't add URL segments. Use them to apply SiteHeader only to app pages, not the landing page. Create `src/app/[locale]/(app)/layout.tsx`: ```tsx import { SiteHeader } from '@/components/site-header' export default function AppLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return (<>{children}) } ``` Move these directories into `(app)/` using `git mv`: - `src/app/[locale]/relationships/` → `src/app/[locale]/(app)/relationships/` - `src/app/[locale]/garden/` → `src/app/[locale]/(app)/garden/` - `src/app/[locale]/contribute/` → `src/app/[locale]/(app)/contribute/` - `src/app/[locale]/plants/` → `src/app/[locale]/(app)/plants/` - `src/app/[locale]/share/` → `src/app/[locale]/(app)/share/` After moving, strip the inline per-page headers from each moved page — they are now handled by SiteHeader: - `(app)/garden/page.tsx`: remove the header div containing `LocaleSwitcher`, `AuthPanel`, `backHome` link, and h1+subtitle. Remove `Link` import from `@/i18n/navigation` if it becomes unused (check if Link is used elsewhere in the file first). - `(app)/contribute/page.tsx`: remove the `back` Link element (the `` near the top of the return). Update e2e smoke tests In `tests/e2e/smoke.test.ts`, replace these two existing tests: - `'home page loads with app heading'` - `'home page has contribute nav link'` With: ```ts test('landing page shows 3 use-case cards', async ({ page }) => { await page.goto('/') await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'power2plant' })).toBeVisible() await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /look up a crop/i })).toBeVisible() await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /plan beds/i })).toBeVisible() await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /my garden/i })).toBeVisible() }) test('plan page has site header with nav', async ({ page }) => { await page.goto('/plan') await expect(page.getByRole('banner')).toBeVisible() await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /look up a crop/i })).toBeVisible() }) ``` ## 7.
